chunks: Hanan ibn Sadeer from Abu Sara al-Ghazzal from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
Allah Mighty and Majestic Said: 'Son of Adam! Keep away from what I prohibited upon you, and you will be among the most devout of the people.'
ai.seo_question: How does avoiding Allah's prohibitions lead to becoming the most devout person?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this Qudsi hadith to define *wara'* (scrupulousness) not merely as avoiding major sins, but as a comprehensive ethical vigilance against all divine prohibitions. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that true piety is rooted in meticulous adherence to God's commands, serving as the foundational metric for spiritual elevation.

en.hubeali:
Hanan Bin Sadeyr, from Abu Sara Al Gazzal, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said: ‘Son of Adam<sup>as</sup>! Keep away from what I<sup>saww</sup> Prohibited upon you (in order for) you to become from the most devout of the people’.
en.sarwar: 7. Hanan ibn Sadir has narrated from abu Sara al-Ghazzal from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, ‘O son of Adam, stay away from what 1 have made unlawful to you, you then will be of the people who restrain themselves from worldly matters the most.’”
